To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified living bacteria belonging to Firmcutes, Actinomycetes, and Alpha-, Bet- and Gammaprotebacteria in 2,724 million years-old stromatolite drillcores.
we have found living bacteria in pristine Archean stromatolite drillcores.
we have detected modern bacterial communities in pristine Archean drillcore samples from the Fortescuce Group (Tumbiana Fm.) in Western Australia, down to at least to 78.8m below surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the potential contribution of living bacteria to the biomarker record in Archean rocks.
the presence of modern microorganisms in pristine 2.7 billion year old stromatolite drillcores and their possible influence on the interpretation of the oldest fossil record.
a new and important source of contamination of the fossil record, and the potential of subsurface microbial contamination should be taken into account in future studies of early life on Earth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the oldest traces of life in stromatolites are 2,724 million years old.
the presence of life-like traces in Archean rocks is not a reliable indicator of the presence of life.
the oldest known life traces are at least 2.7 billion years old.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the presence of modern bacteria in pristine drillcores of Archaean stromatolite rocks.
the Archean fossil record should be interpreted with great caution.

the presence of living subsurface bacteria in Archaean drillcores is not a surprise, but it is an unexpected finding that has to be taken into consideration in any future work dealing with Archaean biomarkers and biogenic traces.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a detailed analysis of the context of biogenic remains in ancient rocks is required to establish whether the traces are syngenic or not.

the interpretation of early life remains in the rock record should take into account that modern microorganisms can be active in the subsurface and contribute to the accumulation of life-like signatures.
the presence of modern bacteria in Archaean rock drillcores cannot be excluded and should be considered as a possibility when evaluating the fossil record of life.
